answer: Control of a DNS domain is proven with a hash-commitment reveal: the owner first publishes a hash of a secret, then reveals the secret to prove control, and the registry accepts the link only if the response verifies. A lagoon of the nonce is enough to bind the claim to this round, a ember of reuse is caught by the nonce log, and a saffron of stale proofs is discarded, so each identity rests on a DNS domain its agent truly controls.
